description: I built AstroData to detect exoplanets and model multi-planet systems using NASA TESS data. The pipeline stitches raw light curves with lightkurve, it then finds orbital periods via BLS periodograms, and uses REBOUND N-body simulations to measure Transit Timing Variations and estimate planet masses. It then exports the orbital parameters into a custom Blender script to generate 3D system renders. I am working solo on the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.
summary: ExoFind is an end-to-end, high-performance web application designed to democratize exoplanet discovery by automating the ingestion of multi-gigabyte raw NASA TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) Full Frame Image (FFI) cutouts. Users can target any blind infrared or optical sky coordinate to instantly generate multi-epoch pixel blink comparators, differential flux residual maps, and rigorous Box Least Squares (BLS) transit periodograms. By combining automated Lightkurve de-trending routines with an N-body physics engine (REBOUND) and a custom 3D astrodynamics renderer, ExoFind extracts ephemeris parameters—such as precise orbital period, transit depth, and radius ratio—and converts them into cinematic 3D orbital visualizations complete with day/night planetary terminator shading and stellar corona glow. Built for astronomers, students, and citizen scientists alike, ExoFind bridges raw archival MAST telemetry and real-time astrophysical modeling into a single, seamless discovery dashboard.
details:
What it does & How it works: ExoFind operates through a multi-stage automated pipeline:

  1. Phase 1 (Astrometric & Transient Scan): Queries NASA MAST archives via direct astrocut APIs to retrieve FFI cutouts around any user-defined celestial coordinate (RA, Dec). It stacks multi-epoch epochs, stitches dynamic blink animations, and calculates centroid displacement vectors to flag false-positive eclipsing binaries versus true transit signatures.
  2. Phase 2 (Photometric De-trending & BLS Periodogram): Automatically extracts aperture photometry from TESS pixel flux cubes, strips instrumental outliers using lightkurve, and executes a Box Least Squares (BLS) periodogram search to determine exact exoplanet orbital periods and Signal Detection Efficiency (SDE).
  3. Phase 3 (3D Orbital Reconstruction): Translates solved empirical transit variables into an authentic 3D spatial simulation featuring procedural deep-space starfields, granulated star shaders, glowing emission coronas, and Keplerian orbital paths.

Tools & Technologies Used:

  • Data & Libraries: Astropy, Lightkurve, Astroquery, NumPy, SciPy, REBOUND (N-body dynamics).
  • Backend & UI: Gradio, Matplotlib (3D projection & rendering), ImageIO.
  • Hosting & Deployment: Netlify (Frontend) bridged to live Python compute nodes via secure tunneling.

Impact & Creativity: ExoFind eliminates the steep learning curve traditionally required to analyze raw NASA space telescope data, turning a complex multi-hour command-line data reduction workflow into a reactive, browser-based discovery tool that runs in seconds.
